correctness.rationale: From the killed reflection-principle kernel, S(t)=erf(L/sqrt(4Dt)) and q(t)=[erfc(L/sqrt(4Dt))-erfc(3L/sqrt(4Dt))]/2 are exact. The finite-mean stationary age-count formula is binomial times q^k(S-q)^(N-k)dt/mu_N for N>=3. With y=L^2/(4Dt), y_N=[erfc^-1(1/N)]^2~log N, mu_N~L^2/(4D y_N), and y=y_N+w, Np~e^-w, Nq~e^-w/2. Uniform bounds away from that layer allow convergence of both fixed-k and total positive-count integrals. Their evaluations give respectively 1/(k3^k) and log(3/2), with Gamma(k,3/2) conditional trigger-age variable; finite quadrature independently corroborated 35 identities, without purporting to prove the limits.

originality.rationale: The novel assertion is a sharp endpoint layer beyond the fixed mirror boundary -L: (log N) P(K=k) -> 1/(k 3^k), a logarithmic-series conditional count, and a Gamma trigger-age conditional law. The close full-text source proves the underlying finite-N renewal formula and first-order large-N extrema and a distinct shrinking-centre count law, but does not state or already logically derive these sharp consequences without a separate nonuniform boundary-layer argument. Searches of relevant literature and an indexed mathematics research corpus identified no equivalent quantitative theorem. Residual risk is explicitly retained for the unpublished/unchecked supplement and possible broad implications of exact representations.
